Getting Around Korea 2026: Complete Transportation Guide

How to get around Seoul and Korea — subway, bus, taxi, KTX, and everything in between. T-money cards, apps, prices, and practical tips.

⏱ 9 min read · 🇰🇷 Seoul, Korea · Updated 2026

Getting Around Korea — One of the World's Best Transit Systems

Korea has some of the world's most efficient, affordable, and extensive public transportation. Seoul's subway system alone has 23 lines covering virtually every corner of the city. High-speed rail connects major cities in hours. And when public transit isn't convenient, taxis are affordable and plentiful. If you're used to struggling with public transport in other Asian cities, Korea will be a revelation.

🎫 The T-Money Card — Your Transit Essential

The T-money card is a rechargeable transit card used on subways, buses, and some taxis across Korea. It's the single most important thing to get when you arrive.

  • Where to buy: Any GS25 or 7-Eleven convenience store. Cost: ₩3,000 for the card.
  • Where to recharge: Same convenience stores, or at subway station machines
  • Discount: Saves ₩100 per subway/bus ride vs cash fare
  • Transfer discount: Free transfers between subway and bus within 30 minutes
  • Taxis: Many Seoul taxis accept T-money payment
  • Refund: Unused balance refundable at convenience stores (minus ₩500 service fee)
💡 T-money tip: Recharge at least ₩20,000–₩30,000 at a time. Running out mid-journey is a hassle. The subway machines accept cash only; convenience stores accept cash and card.

🚇 Seoul Metropolitan Subway

Seoul's subway is the backbone of the city's transport. 23 lines, 800+ stations, operating from 5:30am to midnight (last train varies by station and day). Clean, air-conditioned, punctual, and with announcements in Korean, English, Chinese, and Japanese.

Key Lines for Tourists

  • Line 2 (Green): The circular line — hits Hongdae, Gangnam, Myeongdong area, and connects to most other lines
  • Line 3 (Orange): Gyeongbokgung, Anguk (Bukchon), Insadong area
  • Line 4 (Blue): Myeongdong, Seoul Station, Dongdaemun
  • Line 9 (Gold): Express line from Gimpo Airport to Gangnam — very fast
  • Sinbundang Line: Gangnam area and south Seoul, very modern

Useful Apps

  • Naver Maps: Best overall navigation for Korea. Real-time transit, walking, driving. English available.
  • Kakao Maps: Strong alternative. Better for some local business info.
  • Subway Korea: Dedicated subway map app with route planning.

🚌 Bus System

Seoul's buses are color-coded and complement the subway well, especially for cross-city routes the subway doesn't cover efficiently.

  • Blue buses (간선): Main arterial routes across the city. Most useful for tourists.
  • Green buses (지선): Neighborhood feeder routes connecting to subway stations.
  • Yellow buses (순환): City center circular routes (Jongno, Jung-gu area).
  • Red buses (광역): Express routes to suburbs and satellite cities.

Bus stops have digital displays showing next bus arrival in English. Pay with T-money when boarding. Free transfer to/from subway within 30 minutes.

🚕 Taxis

Seoul taxis are affordable, metered, and plentiful — especially near subway stations and hotels. The base fare is ₩4,800 (standard cab) with ₩100 added per 131m after the initial distance.

Types of Taxis

  • General taxi (일반택시): Silver, white, or various colors. Standard fare. Most common.
  • Deluxe taxi (모범택시): Black cars, more professional drivers, higher price (₩7,000 base)
  • Kakao T Taxi: Ride-hailing app — hail any standard taxi through the app. The app shows English destination so you don't need to speak Korean.
💡 Taxi tip: Download the Kakao T app before you go. Type your destination in English and show the driver the screen — it displays Korean. This eliminates all language barriers. Night surcharge (20–40% extra) applies midnight–4am and during peak hours.

🚄 KTX — High Speed Rail

Korea's KTX (Korea Train Express) is one of the world's best high-speed rail systems. Connecting major cities at up to 305 km/h:

  • Seoul → Busan: 2h 15min (₩59,800 standard)
  • Seoul → Gyeongju: 2h 10min
  • Seoul → Gwangju: 1h 33min
  • Seoul → Daejeon: 50min

Book on the KORAIL website or Korail Talk app. Seat reservations required — trains sell out on weekends and holidays. The KR Pass (multiple-day unlimited travel pass) is available for tourists and can be good value for heavy rail users.

✈️ Getting to/from Incheon Airport

  • AREX Express Train: 43 minutes from Incheon Airport to Seoul Station. ₩9,500. Most convenient.
  • AREX All-Stop: About 66 minutes, stops at more stations. ₩4,150.
  • Airport Limousine Bus: Direct to major hotel areas. ₩16,000–₩20,000. Takes 60–90 minutes depending on traffic.
  • Taxi: About 60–80 minutes to central Seoul. ₩65,000–₩85,000. Premium comfort but expensive.

🚲 Bikes & Other Options

  • Seoul Bike (따릉이): Public bike share system. ₩1,000/hour. Great for Han River rides. App required.
  • Electric scooters: Multiple rental apps (Kick Going, Lime). Useful for short urban trips.
  • Intercity buses: Express buses to cities not on KTX routes. Book at major bus terminals (Express Bus Terminal, Dong Seoul Terminal).
